title: Power Systems
tagline: Per-unit analysis, transmission lines, power flow, faults, stability, dispatch and protection
summary: The electric power system is the largest machine ever built. This course models generators, transformers, lines and loads, solves the power-flow problem, calculates symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults, analyses stability, and studies economic dispatch, frequency control, protection and the modern smart grid.

chapters.title: Power system structure and per-unit analysis
chapters.summary: Generation, transmission and distribution, one-line diagrams and the per-unit system.

chapters.title: Transmission line parameters
chapters.summary: Resistance, inductance and capacitance of overhead lines and cables.

chapters.title: Transmission line models
chapters.summary: Short, medium and long line models, ABCD parameters, surge impedance loading and voltage regulation.

chapters.title: Power flow
chapters.summary: The bus admittance matrix, the power-flow equations, Gauss–Seidel and Newton–Raphson solution, and control of power flow.

chapters.title: Symmetrical faults
chapters.summary: Transients in RL circuits, synchronous machine reactances, fault currents and the bus impedance matrix.

chapters.title: Symmetrical components and unsymmetrical faults
chapters.summary: Symmetrical components, sequence networks, and single line-to-ground, line-to-line and double line-to-ground faults.

chapters.title: Power system stability
chapters.summary: The swing equation, the equal-area criterion, and transient and small-signal stability.

chapters.title: Economic dispatch and frequency control
chapters.summary: Economic dispatch, unit commitment, load–frequency control and automatic generation control.

chapters.title: Protection and the smart grid
chapters.summary: Relays, circuit breakers and protection schemes, and the integration of renewables, storage and smart-grid technologies.
